title: Does the Financial Experience of SEC Regional Directors Impact SEC Investigations?
eligible_reason: Staggered binary treatment at the SEC-regional-office level (office led by a director with practical financial experience). Two offices switch on with pre-periods (Atlanta, office 1, from 2010; Fort Worth, office 5, from calendar 2011 / fiscal 2012), two offices are treated from the first sample year and later switch off (Boston, office 2, off in 2014; Los Angeles, office 6, off in 2008), seven offices are never treated. Table 9, Panel B (b_other_entities.do lines 30 and 69) regresses the winsorized number of investigations opened per office-year on the binary fin_exp indicator with office and year fixed effects and NO controls, clustered by office (N = 121 = 11 offices x 2004-2014): this satisfies every PROTOCOL rule (static TWFE, binary treatment, >= 2 adoption cohorts with pre and post observations, never-treated comparison units). All other main specifications (Table 4A col 1, Tables 5-8, 10, 11) are firm-year regressions that add 10 time-varying firm controls and an additive Fama-French-48 industry FE and are therefore ineligible (near-miss type). Caveats for the eligible spec: only 11 clusters; two always-treated units whose switched-off years must be dropped (Hull footnote 6); the office-year investigation counts are built from a proprietary investigations file that is NOT in the package, so replication requires author contact.
design_notes: Firm-level analysis data (B_MS_Data_redacted.dta): 37,920 firm-years, 6,934 Compustat firms, fyear 2004-2014, 11 SEC regional offices (office_area), 35 director-years (director_id_eoy). Treatment construction (b_stata_cleaning.do lines 195-206): treatment_group = office ever led by a director with financial experience (avg_fin_exp > 0); post_period = fin_experience_eoy == 1; treatment_post = treatment_group x post_period, which equals fin_experience_eoy. Pattern by office x fyear verified with pandas: office 1 = 0 through 2009, 1 from 2010; office 5 = 0 through 2011, 1 from 2012; office 2 = 1 in 2004-2012 (no 2013 obs), 0 in 2014; office 6 = 1 in 2004-2007, 0 from 2008; offices 3,4,7,8,9,10,11 always 0. Main spec (B_MS_Analyses.do line 18): reghdfe investigation_opened treatment_post + 10 controls, absorb(fyear office_area ff48), cluster(director_id_eoy); the published log (Analysis_Log.smcl) gives coef 0.01628 (SE 0.00347), N 37,920, 35 clusters. Robustness: logit and firthlogit (nonlinear), stacked DiD (b_stacked_did.do: cohorts 2010 Atlanta and 2011 Fort Worth with never-treated controls, [-5,5] windows, FE fyear#group_id office_area#group_id ff48#group_id; and a reverse 'un-treatment' stack for Boston 2013 and LA 2007), IV (ivreg2), firm FE added (absorb fyear office_area ff48 gvkey), entropy-balanced pweights. Office-level analysis (b_other_entities.do): investigation-level file SECInvestigations_manipulated.xlsx collapsed to office_started x year counts (2004-2014, office_started_num != 0), winsor2 at 1/99, fin_exp = 1 for office 1 if year > 2009, office 2 if year < 2014, office 5 if year > 2010, office 6 if year < 2008; column 2 drops investigations matched to public-company IDs (pub_co_id.dta).
n_adoption_cohorts_note: Switch-on cohorts with pre-periods: Atlanta (2010) and Fort Worth (2011 by calendar year of investigation opening in the office-level file; fiscal 2012 in the firm-level file). Boston and Los Angeles are treated from the first sample year (2004) and switch off (2014 and 2008): no pre-period, so they count as always-treated after dropping switched-off years.
modern_estimator_note: Stacked regression (Cengiz et al. 2019 / Baker, Larcker and Wang 2022, code adapted from John Barrios) is the only alternative estimator; no CSA, BJS, SA or dCDH.
preferred_spec_note: The paper's preferred estimate is the firm-level Table 4, Panel A, column 1 (ineligible: controls + industry FE). The eligible office-year specifications are a supplementary analysis (Table 9, Panel B).

specs.sample_condition: year 2004-2014; office_started_num != 0; one row per office-year (counter==1)
specs.notes: Treatment switches off for offices 2 (2014) and 6 (2008): drop those office-years per PROTOCOL; the two offices then have no untreated periods (always-treated). Only 11 clusters; leverage screen (effective clusters >= 10, max share <= 0.25) is borderline. Estimated with reg, not reghdfe.

data_files_note: The office-year investigation counts for the eligible Table 9B specs come from SECInvestigations_manipulated.xlsx and pub_co_id.dta, which are not shipped (hand-collected / FOIA / obtained from other authors; README says to contact those authors). The firm-level outcome investigation_opened is also removed. Replication of any eligible or near-miss spec therefore requires author-provided data.
software_notes: Stata (reghdfe, firthlogit, ebalance, ivreg2, winsor2) for analysis; SAS (B_Master_MS.sas) for raw data assembly from Compustat, CRSP, Audit Analytics, IBES.
priority_note: Eligible office-year TWFE (Table 9, Panel B, 2 columns) but the investigation data are absent from the package; author contact needed. Published coefficients recovered from the shipped Stata log.
screener_notes: Screened from package only (no article text). Fort Worth adoption year differs between the firm-level file (fiscal 2012) and the office-level code (calendar year > 2010, i.e., 2011); b_stacked_did.do also uses cohort 2011. Treatment switches off for Boston (2014) and Los Angeles (2008). The firm-level design would be a near-miss (controls + ff48 FE) if Table 9B did not exist.
